outcome: hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes, and low platelets (HELLP) syndrome
duration of neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) stays
cohort: The study included 74 participants, with 37 clinically diagnosed with preeclampsia and 37 normotensive pregnant women.
finding: Preeclampsia is associated with significant hematological changes, including lower platelet counts and elevated bleeding time, INR, APTT, PT, fibrinogen, ALP, and D-dimer levels, as well as adverse maternal (higher cesarean sections) and neonatal outcomes (lower birth weights and increased NICU admissions).
mod_finding: The preeclampsia group had a significantly higher rate of cesarean sections (65%) compared to the normotensive group (24%).
birth_weight: Mean 2.3 kg in the preeclampsia group vs. 2.5 kg in the normotensive group.
